Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Johnson, CEO; Maria Garcia, CFO; and David Lee, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas.

First, let's discuss our sales guidance, forecast, and trends by segment for the next quarter and full year. As previously stated, we are reaffirming our full-year revenue guidance of $76 billion. While the PC Client Computing Group (CCG) segment faces headwinds, the strong performance of Network and Edge Group (NEX) and the Data Center and AI Group (DCAI), particularly in hyperscale, is expected to offset these challenges. Furthermore, we anticipate improved performance across most segments in the second half of the year.

For Q2 2024, we are guiding for revenue of $18 Billion, which is down 2% sequentially. The anticipated sequential decline of 2% reflects a combination of factors, including the tail end of a seasonal dip in CCG and strategic inventory management across key sectors. We maintain confidence in achieving our full-year targets due to expected improvements in the latter half of the year.

Breaking it down by segment, in Client Computing Group (CCG), while facing initial headwinds, we expect CCG revenue to increase substantially in the second half of the year, contributing approximately $32 billion to the full-year revenue target. This optimism is based on several key drivers, including a return to normal seasonality, where we anticipate a traditional back-to-school and holiday season surge in PC demand, commencing in Q3. Historical data indicates a potential 18% increase in CCG revenue between Q2 and Q3, primarily driven by the consumer segment. We believe this recovery will be stronger than initially anticipated, given the prolonged PC refresh cycle. We are also seeing OEM inventory burn subsiding. Over the past two quarters, OEMs have been actively reducing excess inventory. We believe this process is nearing completion, paving the way for increased order volume in Q3 and Q4. Internal estimates suggest a 12% increase in OEM demand for StellarTech processors in the second half of the year as they replenish their stock to meet anticipated market demand. Finally, the ramp of our 13th Gen Raptor Lake processors is progressing according to plan, and we are seeing strong adoption in the gaming and creator segments. Early data suggests that Raptor Lake is outperforming previous generations in terms of average selling price (ASP), with a 7% increase in ASP compared to Alder Lake. The ongoing expansion of our Alder Lake family into the value segment is also expected to contribute to volume growth. For Q3, we project a 15% increase in revenue year-over-year to approximately $7.5 billion, driven by these factors.

For our Data Center and AI Group (DCAI), DCAI remains a critical growth engine for StellarTech, projected to contribute approximately $28 billion in revenue for the full year. We are particularly bullish about the hyperscale segment, which is experiencing sustained growth. Our relationships with leading hyperscale cloud providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) remain strong. We are seeing accelerated adoption of our Ice Lake and Sapphire Rapids processors in their data centers. We have secured several multi-year contracts with these customers, providing revenue visibility and long-term growth potential. We project a 25% year-over-year increase in revenue from our top three hyperscale customers. The easing of component supply constraints is enabling us to fulfill a backlog of orders from data center customers. We expect this trend to continue throughout the year, supporting our growth trajectory. Lead times for key components, such as power management ICs, have decreased by approximately 30% compared to the previous quarter. The ramp of our 4th Gen StellarTech Xeon Scalable processors (Sapphire Rapids) is progressing well. While the initial ramp was slower than anticipated due to platform validation delays, we are now seeing increased adoption across various segments, including hyperscale, enterprise, and government. The performance and efficiency gains offered by Sapphire Rapids are resonating with customers, particularly those focused on AI and data analytics workloads. We are forecasting a 22% increase in DCAI revenue in Q3, reaching $6.8 billion, driven primarily by Sapphire Rapids adoption and hyperscale demand.

Our Network and Edge Group (NEX) continues to be a standout performer, expected to generate over $9 billion in revenue for the full year. The strength observed in Q1 is expected to persist, driven by several factors, including improving component supply, similar to DCAI, NEX is benefiting from improved component availability, enabling us to fulfill pent-up demand from networking equipment vendors and edge computing solution providers. The continued 5G ramp is driving significant demand for StellarTech's network processors, baseband units, and other networking solutions. We have secured key design wins with leading telecom equipment manufacturers, including Ericsson and Nokia. The transformation at the Edge is creating new opportunities for StellarTech in areas such as industrial automation, retail, and healthcare. We are seeing strong demand for our edge server platforms and AI inference accelerators. We are launching a new "Edge Ready" program to accelerate the adoption of StellarTech-based edge solutions. We anticipate a 18% increase in NEX revenue in Q3, reaching $2.2 billion, fueled by 5G deployments and edge computing adoption.

We reaffirm our expectation for the Accelerated Computing Systems and Graphics Group (AXG) to generate revenue exceeding $1 billion. This growth hinges on the successful launch and ramp of our Alchemist (discrete GPUs), Arctic Sound-M (data center GPUs), Ponte Vecchio (high-performance computing GPU), and Blockscale (blockchain accelerator) products. We are focused on expanding the availability of our Arc Alchemist GPUs through partnerships with OEMs and retailers. We are also working to improve driver stability and performance to enhance the user experience. We are investing in marketing and community outreach to build brand awareness and drive adoption. We are targeting data centers and cloud gaming providers with our Arctic Sound-M GPUs, working with key partners to optimize workloads for our architecture. We are focused on delivering Ponte Vecchio to our key high-performance computing customers, including national laboratories and research institutions. And we are targeting blockchain infrastructure providers with our Blockscale ASICs. We anticipate a significant ramp in AXG revenue in Q3, reaching approximately $350 million, driven by increased availability of Alchemist GPUs and initial shipments of Arctic Sound-M.

Finally, we expect Mobileye to experience strong growth in the second half of the year, driven by the ramp of new ADAS (Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems) and autonomous driving solutions. We are securing new design wins with leading automakers, expanding our market share. We forecast a 12% increase in Mobileye revenue in Q3 to $520 million, fueled by new customer deployments and increased ADAS adoption rates.

Intel Foundry Services (IFS) is strategically important to StellarTech's long-term growth. We expect to see increased revenue in the second half of the year as we secure new customers and ramp production on our advanced process technologies. We are actively engaged with potential customers across various segments, including mobile, automotive, and high-performance computing. We project a 25% increase in IFS revenue in Q3 to $200 million as we begin to see revenue from early customer engagements.

North America remains a strong market for StellarTech, particularly in the data center and enterprise segments. We are seeing increased demand for our products in Europe, driven by investments in digital infrastructure and the adoption of AI. Asia-Pacific is a key growth market for StellarTech, particularly in China and Southeast Asia. We are focused on expanding our presence in these regions through strategic partnerships and localized product offerings.

Our ability to achieve our full-year revenue guidance hinges on our ability to execute our product roadmap and deliver on our commitments to customers. We are actively managing our supply chain to mitigate risks and ensure that we have the components we need to meet demand. We are continuing to invest in research and development to drive innovation in our core technologies and create new growth opportunities, and we are committed to maintaining cost discipline and improving operational efficiency.

Next, I’d like to cover our Q1 2024 net margin performance and diluted earnings per share (EPS) results, followed by an outlook for Q2 2024 and the full fiscal year. Our Q1 2024 diluted EPS came in at $0.87, a significant $0.07 above our previously communicated guidance of $0.80. This positive variance was primarily driven by a combination of factors, all contributing to a robust net margin performance. We saw a notable increase in gross profit margin, expanding by 120 basis points to 42.5% compared to 41.3% in Q4 2023 and 40.8% in Q1 2023. This improvement was fueled by several key initiatives, including our ongoing efforts to diversify our supplier base and negotiate more favorable terms, which yielded tangible results. We achieved a 5% reduction in raw material costs across our core product lines, directly impacting cost of goods sold. We also successfully shifted our sales towards higher-margin products, specifically within our premium "Alpha" line, which accounted for 28% of total revenue, up from 22% in Q4 2023. This strategic shift reflects increased customer demand for our high-value offerings. Finally, investments in automation and process improvements at our Atlanta manufacturing facility resulted in a 7% reduction in labor costs per unit produced, further contributing to gross margin expansion. We also demonstrated effective cost control, achieving a slight decrease in operating expenses as a percentage of revenue. OpEx came in at 28.2% of revenue, compared to 28.5% in Q4 2023. This was largely due to implementing a data-driven approach to our marketing campaigns, focusing on channels with higher conversion rates and reducing inefficient spending. For instance, our digital marketing ROI improved by 15% due to targeted campaigns. We also streamlined our administrative processes and reduced redundant functions, resulting in a 3% decrease in general and administrative expenses. Our performance varied by region. North America continued to be our strongest market, accounting for 55% of total revenue with a 15% increase in Q1 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by strong demand for our new product launches. In Europe, we saw a more moderate growth of 8%, impacted by economic headwinds and currency fluctuations. However, our APAC region showed promising growth of 12%, fueled by increased adoption of our products in emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia. Beyond the tactical cost-saving measures, our strong Q1 performance also reflects the success of our strategic initiatives. Our focus on enhancing customer experience and building brand loyalty is paying off. We saw a 10% increase in customer retention rates, leading to higher lifetime value. Our investments in digital technologies are streamlining our operations, improving customer engagement, and driving revenue growth. For example, our e-commerce platform saw a 20% increase in sales, driven by improved user experience and personalized recommendations.

While we are pleased with our Q1 results, we anticipate a more challenging environment in Q2 2024, leading to a projected EPS of $0.70, a $0.17 sequential decrease. This guidance reflects the following factors. We expect gross profit margin to decline to 41%, a decrease of 150 basis points sequentially. This is primarily due to facing inflationary pressures on certain raw materials, particularly for components sourced from overseas. We project a 7% increase in these costs in Q2. We also plan to implement strategic promotional campaigns to drive volume growth and maintain market share in a more competitive landscape. This will impact gross margin in the short term. We anticipate an increase in operating expenses as a percentage of revenue, rising to 29% from 28.2% in Q1. This is driven by launching several new products in Q2, requiring increased marketing and sales investments, and accelerating our R&D efforts to develop innovative products and maintain our competitive edge.

Despite the expected challenges in Q2, we are maintaining our full-year EPS guidance of $3.60. This reflects our confidence in our long-term growth strategy and our ability to navigate the evolving market dynamics. We anticipate that our strategic initiatives, including cost optimization efforts, product innovation, and market expansion, will drive improved performance in the second half of the year. We are forecasting stronger performance in Q3 and Q4 as new products begin to gain traction and the impact of our cost-saving initiatives becomes more pronounced. Specifically, we project a recovery in gross margin in Q3 and Q4 as the impact of promotional activities subsides and the benefits of our supply chain optimization efforts become more visible.

I’ll now pass it over to Maria to walk through the numbers in more detail.

Maria Garcia, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with our operating margin results. StellarTech's overall operating margin for Q2 2023 reflects a complex interplay of strategic investments, product transitions, and market dynamics. While certain business units demonstrated robust growth and improved profitability, others faced headwinds due to ramp-up costs, increased R&D spending, and competitive pressures. A key takeaway is the significant impact of the 10-nanometer and Intel 7 process technologies on overall profitability, as well as the firm's commitment to investing in future growth areas like AXG and IFS. Overall, StellarTech's Q2 2023 operating margin was 22.5%, down from 28.7% in Q2 2022, and slightly below the previous guidance of 23.0%

Looking at the Client Computing Group (CCG), their operating profit was $2.1 Billion, down 34% year-over-year (YoY). The substantial decline in CCG's operating profit is primarily attributed to a 15% decrease in revenue (estimated at $13.5 billion in Q2 2023 compared to $15.9 billion in Q2 2022) reflecting softening PC demand, particularly in the consumer segment in the EMEA and APAC regions. Increased adoption of 10-nanometer and Intel 7 based CPUs, while improving performance, impacted margins negatively due to higher manufacturing costs. This impact is estimated to be around a 3-percentage point reduction in operating margin. Furthermore, strategic investments in next-generation mobile and desktop platforms, including increased validation and pre-launch marketing expenses for the upcoming Meteor Lake architecture, resulted in a further 2-percentage point decline. However, operating profit increased by 8% compared to Q1 2023 due to a slight rebound in PC demand in North America and Europe. CCG's operating profit fell slightly short of the previous quarter's guidance, which projected a 32% YoY decline. This slight miss was due to higher-than-anticipated component costs and a more aggressive promotional environment during the quarter, particular surrounding back-to-school campaigns. While PC demand is expected to remain volatile, CCG's outlook for the second half of 2023 anticipates a modest recovery driven by new product launches and a gradual improvement in the macroeconomic environment.

The Data Center and AI (DCAI) group had an operating profit of $1.7 Billion, flat YoY. Despite a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, DCAI's operating profit remained flat due to several offsetting factors. Increased adoption of 10-nanometer-based Xeon Scalable processors, while driving revenue growth, impacted margins due to higher manufacturing costs and lower initial yields. Factory start-up costs associated with the new Arizona and Ohio facilities also contributed to the margin pressure, accounting for an estimated 1-percentage point decline. Furthermore, increased investments in AI accelerators and next-generation Xeon processors resulted in higher R&D expenses, offsetting the revenue gains. Operating profit increased by 5% compared to Q1 2023, driven by strong demand for cloud-based services and AI workloads. DCAI's operating profit performance aligned with the previous quarter's guidance, reflecting accurate forecasting and effective cost management. DCAI is expected to maintain strong growth momentum in the second half of 2023, driven by continued demand for cloud and AI infrastructure.

The Network and Edge (NEX) group had an operating profit of $366 Million, up 51% YoY. NEX delivered impressive operating profit growth, driven by a 25% increase in revenue to $1.1 Billion. This growth was fueled by strong demand for 5G infrastructure and edge computing solutions, particularly in the telecom and industrial automation sectors. Increased investment in R&D was offset by the higher revenue, and improved product mix resulting in a higher gross margin. Operating profit increased by 18% compared to Q1 2023, reflecting continued momentum in the network and edge markets. NEX significantly exceeded the previous quarter's guidance, which projected a 40% YoY increase in operating profit. This outperformance was due to stronger-than-expected demand for 5G infrastructure in emerging markets. NEX is expected to maintain its strong growth trajectory in the second half of 2023, driven by continued investment in 5G and edge computing technologies.

Mobileye had an operating profit of $148 Million, down 13% YoY. Mobileye's operating profit declined due to increased investments in next-generation autonomous driving platforms. While revenue increased by 10% to $450 million due to increased ADAS adoption, the margin impact of increased R&D offset this. Specifically, development costs for the next-generation EyeQ6 and EyeQ7 systems-on-chip (SoCs) and associated software stacks contributed to the increased expenses. Operating profit decreased by 5% compared to Q1 2023, reflecting the continued impact of increased R&D spending. Mobileye's operating profit performance aligned with the previous quarter's guidance, reflecting accurate forecasting and effective cost management. Mobileye is expected to see improved profitability in the second half of 2023 as the new platforms get closer to launch.

The Accelerated Computing Systems and Graphics (AXG) group had an operating loss of $390 Million, versus an operating loss of $176 Million in Q2 2022. The significant increase in operating loss reflects the ongoing investments in StellarTech's discrete GPU business. New product qualification reserves for the Alchemist and Arctic Sound products, accounting for an estimated $100 Million, significantly impacted the results. Production ramp charges associated with the initial manufacturing runs of these products also contributed to the increased losses. Furthermore, increased R&D spending on future GPU architectures and software development further exacerbated the financial impact. Operating loss increased by 15% compared to Q1 2023, driven by the continued ramp-up of AXG's product portfolio. AXG's operating loss exceeded the previous quarter's guidance, which projected an operating loss of $350 million. This variance was due to higher-than-anticipated production ramp charges and increased marketing expenses associated with the launch of the Alchemist GPUs. AXG is expected to continue to incur operating losses in the near term as it invests in building its discrete GPU business. However, the company anticipates improved profitability in the long term as it gains market share and achieves economies of scale.

Finally, Intel Foundry Services (IFS) had an operating loss of $31 Million, roughly flat YoY. IFS's operating loss remained relatively flat as revenue and gross margin increases were offset by increased investment to build out the custom foundry business. Increased revenue from early customer engagements helped to offset the losses, but the impact of new facility development and workforce expansion continued to weigh on the bottom line. Operating loss decreased slightly compared to Q1 2023, reflecting progress in securing new customer engagements. IFS's operating loss aligned with the previous quarter's guidance, reflecting accurate forecasting and effective cost management. IFS is expected to continue to invest heavily in building its foundry business, with the goal of achieving profitability in the long term.

StellarTech's Q2 2023 operating margin performance highlights the challenges and opportunities facing the company as it undergoes a significant transformation. The company's commitment to investing in future growth areas like AXG and IFS is expected to drive long-term value creation, but will likely weigh on profitability in the near term. The successful execution of StellarTech's IDM 2.0 strategy, including the ramp-up of its advanced manufacturing technologies and the expansion of its foundry business, will be critical to improving its overall financial performance. The company's ability to navigate the current macroeconomic headwinds and maintain its market leadership in key segments will also be crucial to its long-term success.

Now, moving to gross margin. Our Q1 2024 gross margin performance significantly exceeded expectations, landing at 53.0%, a 100 basis point beat against our guidance of 52.0%. This positive result stems from a confluence of factors, primarily driven by operational efficiencies in our manufacturing processes and strategic cost reductions within our fabrication facilities. This translates to approximately $1.27 billion in gross profit on a revenue base of $2.4 billion, representing a 15% increase in Q1 revenue year-over-year to $2.4 billion from $2.08 billion in Q1 2023. Key drivers contributing to this positive performance include a targeted initiative focused on enhancing wafer fabrication processes for our legacy 14nm node yielded substantial improvements. Specifically, we saw a 3% increase in good die per wafer, directly contributing approximately 60 basis points to the gross margin improvement. This was achieved through a combination of advanced process control (APC) implementation and rigorous defect reduction programs. We also implemented a comprehensive cost optimization program across our global fabrication network, focusing on energy consumption reduction, material waste minimization, and supply chain optimization. These initiatives yielded significant savings, contributing approximately 40 basis points to the gross margin beat. For example, a renegotiated contract with our primary silicon wafer supplier, facilitated by increased volume commitments, resulted in a 5% reduction in wafer costs. Finally, while not the primary driver, a slightly more favorable product mix in Q1, with a higher proportion of higher-margin products (e.g., specialized embedded solutions) compared to initial projections, contributed modestly to the outperformance. The embedded solutions segment, particularly within the automotive sector, experienced a surge in demand, resulting in a 12% revenue increase year-over-year.

Our Q1 2024 gross margin of 53.0% represents a 150 basis point increase compared to the 51.5% reported in Q4 2023. This QoQ improvement is primarily attributable to the aforementioned manufacturing yield improvements and factory cost reduction initiatives, which were still in early stages of implementation during Q4 2023. Compared to the 50.0% gross margin reported in Q1 2023, the Q1 2024 result represents a significant 300 basis point improvement. This YoY increase is a testament to the success of our strategic investments in manufacturing process optimization, cost control measures, and a more focused product portfolio. In Q1 2023, we were still grappling with supply chain disruptions and higher raw material costs, which negatively impacted our profitability. The strategic decision to insource certain critical components also began to yield positive results in Q1 2024, contributing to the YoY improvement.

However, looking ahead to Q2 2024, we are guiding for a gross margin of 51.0%, reflecting a sequential decrease of approximately 200 basis points. This anticipated decline is primarily attributable to planned product mix shifts, specifically a higher proportion of revenue derived from our newer 10-nanometer and Intel 7 based products, coupled with the establishment of Raptor Lake prequalification reserves. We are ramping up production and shipments of our 10-nanometer and Intel 7 based products in Q2 2024. While these products offer significant performance improvements and command premium pricing, they initially carry lower gross margins due to higher manufacturing costs associated with the newer process nodes. We anticipate that the increased mix of these products will negatively impact the overall gross margin by approximately 120 basis points. Specifically, we expect a 25% increase in 10nm and Intel 7 product revenue in Q2. As we prepare for the launch of our next-generation Raptor Lake processors, we are establishing prequalification reserves to account for potential defects or performance issues identified during the pre-launch testing phase. These reserves will negatively impact the Q2 gross margin by approximately 80 basis points. This is a standard practice in the semiconductor industry to ensure product quality and reliability at launch.

We are actively implementing several mitigation strategies, including continuing to refine our manufacturing processes for both legacy and advanced process nodes, with a focus on further improving yields and reducing costs, actively managing our pricing strategy to optimize profitability across our product portfolio, taking into account competitive dynamics and market demand, continuously working to optimize our supply chain, negotiating favorable terms with our suppliers and diversifying our sourcing to mitigate potential disruptions, and we anticipate a ramp-up of higher margin products, particularly in the server and data center segments, in the second half of 2024, which will help offset the pressure on gross margins from the increased mix of 10nm and Intel 7 based products.

The North American market continues to be a strong contributor to our overall revenue and profitability, driven by robust demand for our high-performance computing solutions. However, we are observing increased price sensitivity in the Asian market, particularly in the consumer electronics segment. We are actively adjusting our pricing strategy and product offerings to remain competitive in this region.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on our P&L guidance for next quarter. Our revenue guidance for the second quarter of 2024 is set at $18 billion. This reflects a cautiously optimistic outlook, representing a 7% increase compared to the $16.8 billion recorded in Q2 2023. This growth is driven primarily by strong performance in our Cloud Services and Enterprise Solutions segments, partially offset by anticipated softness in our legacy hardware business. We expect our Cloud Services division to contribute approximately $7.5 billion to overall Q2 revenue, a robust 12% increase year-over-year. This growth is fueled by the continued adoption of our AI-powered cloud platform, "SynergyCloud," particularly within the healthcare and financial services industries. We've seen a significant uptick in enterprise clients migrating critical workloads to SynergyCloud due to its enhanced security features and scalability. Specifically, our new "SynergyAI" suite, which offers advanced machine learning capabilities integrated directly into the cloud infrastructure, is gaining significant traction. We are observing a higher average revenue per user (ARPU) in this segment, driven by add-on services and premium support packages. Our Enterprise Solutions segment, encompassing software and consulting services, is projected to generate $6.0 billion in revenue for Q2, representing an 8% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth is attributed to increased demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our new suite of supply chain management software. A major contract win with "Global Logistics Corp," a leading logistics provider, will contribute approximately $300 million to this segment's revenue in Q2. The Hardware Sales segment is expected to contribute $4.5 billion, a decrease of 2% year-over-year. This reflects the ongoing shift in customer preference towards cloud-based solutions and a general slowdown in the PC and server markets. We are strategically managing this decline by focusing on high-margin, specialized hardware solutions targeting niche markets like high-performance computing (HPC) and edge computing. Our new line of "QuantumEdge" servers, designed for edge AI applications, is showing promising early adoption.

We anticipate strong performance in North America, driven by robust enterprise spending and government initiatives focused on digital transformation. The European market is expected to show moderate growth, influenced by macroeconomic uncertainties and regulatory headwinds. We are closely monitoring the impact of the Digital Services Act (DSA) on our European operations. Asia-Pacific remains a key growth market, with strong demand for cloud services and enterprise solutions. We are investing heavily in expanding our data center footprint and sales teams in this region, particularly in Southeast Asia and India. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q2 revenue in the APAC region year-over-year, reaching $3.2 billion.

Our gross margin guidance for Q2 2024 is 51%. This represents a slight improvement compared to the 50.5% gross margin reported in Q2 2023. This increase is primarily driven by the higher proportion of revenue from Cloud Services, which typically carries higher gross margins, we have implemented several cost optimization initiatives across our supply chain and operations, resulting in lower material costs and improved operational efficiency. For example, consolidating our data center infrastructure in strategically located regions has reduced energy costs by approximately 5%, and the strong demand for our AI-powered cloud solutions allows us to maintain premium pricing, further supporting our gross margins. We are actively managing pricing strategies to balance competitiveness with profitability.

Our strategy of embedding AI capabilities across our product portfolio is proving to be a key differentiator and a driver of revenue growth and margin expansion. We are actively transitioning towards a recurring revenue model by offering subscription-based services and long-term contracts. This provides greater revenue visibility and stability. We are forging strategic partnerships with leading technology providers to expand our ecosystem and offer integrated solutions. Our recent partnership with "DataSecure Inc." to integrate their cybersecurity platform with SynergyCloud is expected to generate significant cross-selling opportunities. We are closely monitoring macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical risks, and supply chain disruptions to proactively mitigate potential impacts on our financial performance. We are also investing in cybersecurity measures to protect our data and systems from cyber threats. An ongoing internal project aimed at optimizing our software development lifecycle and reducing development costs, called Project "Phoenix", should produce a 2% reduction in software development expenses by the end of Q2 as a result of this initiative, and we are investing in upgrading our data center infrastructure with more energy-efficient technologies, including advanced cooling systems and renewable energy sources. This is expected to reduce our data center operating expenses by approximately 3% in Q2.

Now, let me hand things over to David to talk about product and operational progress.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Maria.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances.

Also worth noting is our improvement in sales guidance, forecast, or trend by segment next quarter or full year, as Alex already mentioned.

And we’ve made foundational changes in how we approach P&L guidance for next quarter, particularly on the fulfillment and logistics side.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On the revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, revenue results v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons, could you expand on what’s driving that strength?

Alex Johnson:
Certainly. We achieved a total revenue of $18.4 billion, a figure that modestly surpasses our guidance of $18.0 billion issued last quarter. This positive variance of approximately 2.2% is primarily attributable to exceptional performance within our Network and Edge Group (NEX) business, which more than offset some of the headwinds experienced in other segments. NEX delivered an all-time record quarterly revenue of $2.2 billion, representing a substantial 23% year-over-year (YoY) increase. Sequentially, NEX experienced a robust 15% increase in Q3 revenue compared to Q2's $1.9 billion. This impressive growth was fueled by broad-based strength across all of its product lines: Cloud, Networking, and Edge. Specifically, Cloud infrastructure solutions saw a 28% YoY increase, driven by robust demand from hyperscale data center operators undergoing significant infrastructure upgrades to support AI workloads. Our "Sapphire Rapids" Xeon processors tailored for cloud environments experienced a 35% increase in unit shipments, exceeding internal projections. We believe our competitive pricing strategy, coupled with the performance benefits of our advanced security features, contributed significantly to this success. In Networking, we saw a 19% YoY increase. The adoption rate of our programmable Ethernet switches, particularly the Tofino series, continues to climb as enterprises modernize their networks to handle increasing bandwidth demands. The rollout of 5G infrastructure globally also contributed, with increased demand for our RAN (Radio Access Network) solutions, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region. We secured a significant contract with a major telecom operator in Southeast Asia, projected to contribute approximately $75 million in revenue over the next four quarters. The Edge computing segment witnessed a 21% YoY increase, driven by the burgeoning demand for IoT solutions and industrial automation. Our "Elkhart Lake" platform for industrial PCs saw a 40% increase in adoption, reflecting the growing trend of deploying compute power closer to the edge for real-time data processing and analytics. Turning to the Client Computing Group (CCG), revenue totaled $9.3 billion, representing a 13% YoY decline. This decline was anticipated and factored into our guidance. Several factors contributed to this performance, including the complete ramp-down of our CPU and modem business with Apple, which had a significant impact, accounting for approximately 8 percentage points of the 13% decline. The absence of this revenue stream is now fully reflected in our financials. We observed continued inventory correction among our OEM partners, who are working through excess inventory accumulated during the pandemic-driven PC boom. We estimate this inventory burn reduced our CCG revenue by approximately 3%. We anticipate this correction to largely conclude by the end of Q4, setting the stage for a more normalized demand environment in 2025. We witnessed a softening in consumer and education PC demand, particularly in developed markets like North America and Europe. Inflationary pressures and a shift in consumer spending towards experiences rather than goods are impacting PC purchase decisions. Chromebook sales, heavily reliant on the education sector, saw a 15% YoY decline. We are actively addressing this by focusing on higher-margin premium notebooks and innovative form factors. The Data Center and AI (DCAI) group delivered a strong performance, with revenue reaching $6.0 billion, a 22% YoY increase. This growth was primarily driven by robust demand for our Xeon processors from both hyperscale cloud providers and enterprise customers. Hyperscale demand was particularly strong, with a 25% YoY increase in Xeon processor shipments. The adoption of our "Emerald Rapids" generation of processors, which offer significant performance improvements for AI inference workloads, has been very encouraging. Enterprise demand for Xeon processors also grew significantly, up 18% YoY, driven by the continued modernization of enterprise data centers and the increasing adoption of AI-powered applications. We are seeing strong traction in the financial services and healthcare sectors. Mobileye continued its growth trajectory, achieving all-time record quarterly revenue of $394 million, up 5% YoY. While the growth rate is slower than previous quarters, this is primarily due to supply chain constraints impacting the broader automotive industry. Despite these challenges, Mobileye continues to secure design wins with leading automotive manufacturers, solidifying its position in the advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) market. AXG revenue was $219 million, up 21% YoY. This growth was driven by the ramp-up of our supercompute and Alchemist discrete GPU products. We are seeing strong interest in our Ponte Vecchio GPUs for high-performance computing applications, and our Alchemist GPUs are gaining traction in the gaming market, particularly in the mid-range segment. We are on track to launch our next-generation "Battlemage" GPUs in the first half of 2025. IFS revenue continued its impressive growth, reaching $283 million, up a remarkable 175% YoY. This growth reflects the increasing demand for our foundry services and the successful execution of our IDM 2.0 strategy. We are making significant progress in securing new customers and expanding our manufacturing capacity. We are seeing strong interest from both traditional semiconductor companies and emerging AI chip designers. The primary driver of our outperformance was the exceptional growth in the NEX business, which exceeded our internal projections by approximately $200 million. The strength in NEX was partially offset by slightly weaker-than-expected performance in CCG, primarily due to the accelerated OEM inventory correction. We are closely monitoring inventory levels and working with our OEM partners to ensure a smooth transition to a more normalized demand environment.
